_comment: Expressive evaluation sentences (SPEECH_QUALITY_PLAN.md S0.2). `stem` is spoken ending in '.', '?' and '!' for the punctuation test; neutral/happy/sad/angry are whole sentences whose wording carries the intended emotion, for the emotion-accuracy test. Written for this project; plain ASCII; every text must pass the API's text validator.

sentences.stem: You are coming to the meeting
sentences.neutral: The meeting starts at nine and ends at ten.
sentences.happy: We won the contract! I cannot believe how well it went!
sentences.sad: Nobody came to the meeting. I think it is all over for us now.
sentences.angry: You never read the report! I am sick of explaining everything twice!

sentences.stem: We found the keys in the garden
sentences.neutral: The keys are on the shelf next to the door.
sentences.happy: I found my keys and my wallet! What a lucky morning this is!
sentences.sad: I have searched everywhere for those keys. I just feel so tired and lost.
sentences.angry: You lost the keys again! How many times do I have to say it?

sentences.stem: She said she would call tonight
sentences.neutral: The call is scheduled for seven in the evening.
sentences.happy: She is calling tonight! I have waited so long for this news!
sentences.sad: She said she would call. She never did, and I stopped hoping.
sentences.angry: She promised to call and then ignored me! That is completely unacceptable!

sentences.neutral: The house is two stories tall with a small garden.
sentences.happy: We have a new house at last! The garden is absolutely beautiful!
sentences.sad: We had to leave the house behind. It held every memory I had.
sentences.angry: They took our house without a word! This is an outrage!

sentences.stem: That is the last of the cake
sentences.neutral: The cake is made with flour, eggs, and sugar.
sentences.happy: This cake is amazing! Thank you so much, it is perfect!
sentences.sad: The cake was for her birthday. Nobody is left to eat it now.
sentences.angry: Who ate the whole cake? I told everyone to leave some!

sentences.stem: He is waiting at the station
sentences.neutral: The train to the city leaves every twenty minutes.
sentences.happy: He is here at last! I am so happy to see him again!
sentences.sad: He waited at the station for hours. Nobody ever came for him.
sentences.angry: He is late again! I will not wait for him any longer!

sentences.neutral: The report covers the sales figures for the last quarter.
sentences.happy: You finished the report early! This is wonderful news for the team!
sentences.sad: The report took everything out of me. I do not think it was good enough.
sentences.angry: The report is full of mistakes! Do it again, and do it properly!

sentences.neutral: The weather today is cloudy with light rain in the afternoon.
sentences.happy: It is raining and I love it! Let us go and dance in the puddles!
sentences.sad: Rain again today. The grey sky matches how I feel inside.
sentences.angry: This rain ruined my plans! I am furious about the whole trip!

sentences.stem: They are opening a new shop
sentences.neutral: The shop opens at eight and closes at six.
sentences.happy: The new shop is open! Everything inside is half price today!
sentences.sad: The old shop on our street has closed. It feels so empty without it.
sentences.angry: They tore down my shop for this! I will never forgive that decision!

sentences.neutral: The race begins at noon on the main road.
sentences.happy: She won the race! I am jumping up and down with joy!
sentences.sad: She trained for years and still lost. I could see it break her heart.
sentences.angry: She cheated to win that race! Everyone knows it was not fair!

sentences.neutral: The dog sleeps in the kitchen near the back door.
sentences.happy: My dog is home safe! I am so relieved and happy right now!
sentences.sad: My dog is gone. The house is far too quiet without him.
sentences.angry: The dog ruined my sandwich again! I am so angry I could scream!

sentences.neutral: The exam has forty questions and lasts two hours.
sentences.happy: He passed the exam! We are all so proud of him!
sentences.sad: He failed the exam by one point. He could not even speak about it.
sentences.angry: He copied his answers on the exam! That is cheating and I will report it!

sentences.neutral: My birthday is on the fourteenth of March.
sentences.happy: You remembered my birthday! This is the nicest surprise ever!
sentences.sad: Nobody remembered my birthday this year. I spent it alone.
sentences.angry: You forgot my birthday again! I cannot believe how careless you are!

sentences.neutral: The bus arrives at the corner every fifteen minutes.
sentences.happy: The bus is here, and just in time! What perfect timing today!
sentences.sad: I missed the last bus home. I just sat and cried at the stop.
sentences.angry: The bus is late every single day! This service is a disgrace!

sentences.stem: We are going to the beach
sentences.neutral: The beach is about an hour away by car.
sentences.happy: We are going to the beach! I cannot wait to feel the sun!
sentences.sad: We will never go back to our beach. It is not the same without her.
sentences.angry: You cancelled the beach trip again! I am done making plans with you!

sentences.neutral: The piano in the hall was made in nineteen sixty.
sentences.happy: She plays so beautifully! I could listen to her all night long!
sentences.sad: She stopped playing the piano after he died. The room fell silent.
sentences.angry: Stop banging on that piano! I have asked you a hundred times already!

sentences.neutral: The ring is made of silver and has a small stone.
sentences.happy: He gave me a ring! I said yes, and I am the happiest person alive!
sentences.sad: He gave me a ring and then he left. I still wear it every day.
sentences.angry: He took back the ring! How dare he treat me like that!

sentences.neutral: The baby sleeps for about three hours each afternoon.
sentences.happy: The baby smiled at me today! My heart is overflowing with joy!
sentences.sad: The baby is gone. I wake up every night listening for her cry.
sentences.angry: Do not wake the baby! I told you to be quiet, and you did not listen!

sentences.neutral: The game ended with a score of two to one.
sentences.happy: We won the game! The whole crowd is cheering our names!
sentences.sad: We lost the final game. Everything we worked for slipped away.
sentences.angry: We lost because of your stupid mistake! You threw the whole season away!

sentences.neutral: The office opens at eight thirty every weekday morning.
sentences.happy: You made it just in time! I am so glad you are here!
sentences.sad: You were late, and I waited alone. I stopped expecting you long ago.
sentences.angry: You are late again! Do you have any respect for my time at all?

sentences.neutral: The letter was sent from the city office on Monday.
sentences.happy: The letter came, and it is good news! I got into the program!
sentences.sad: The letter said she was gone. I read it again and again in disbelief.
sentences.angry: The letter is full of lies! I will not accept a single word of it!

sentences.neutral: The flight from Boston lands at four in the afternoon.
sentences.happy: He is coming home tomorrow! I have missed him so very much!
sentences.sad: He is not coming home tomorrow. He will not be coming home at all.
sentences.angry: He is coming home after all this time? He has some nerve!

sentences.neutral: The fence runs along the north side of the property.
sentences.happy: They painted the fence bright yellow! It looks wonderful and cheerful!
sentences.sad: They painted over the old fence where we wrote our names. It is gone.
sentences.angry: They painted my fence without asking! That is my property, not theirs!

sentences.stem: You can see the mountains from here
sentences.neutral: The mountains are about forty miles to the north.
sentences.happy: Look at the mountains! This view is the most beautiful thing I have seen!
sentences.sad: I used to climb those mountains with him. Now I just watch them alone.
sentences.angry: Those mountains are blocked by your ugly building! Take it down at once!

sentences.neutral: The car was built in nineteen ninety and runs well.
sentences.happy: She sold the old car for a great price! We can finally take a holiday!
sentences.sad: She sold the old car, the last thing her father left her.
sentences.angry: She sold my car behind my back! I will never trust her again!

sentences.neutral: The next exit is in three miles on the right.
sentences.happy: We are almost there! I can see the lights of the town!
sentences.sad: We are almost there, but I wish we were not. I dread what we will find.
sentences.angry: We are almost there because you took the wrong road! Look at the time!

sentences.neutral: The letter is four pages long and typed on blue paper.
sentences.happy: He wrote me a long letter! It made me laugh and cry with happiness!
sentences.sad: He wrote a long letter before he left. I keep it under my pillow.
sentences.angry: He wrote a long letter full of excuses! I am not interested in any of them!

sentences.neutral: The garden has roses, tulips, and a small pond.
sentences.happy: The garden looks wonderful! All the flowers are blooming at once!
sentences.sad: The garden looks empty now. Nothing grows where she used to kneel.
sentences.angry: Who trampled my garden? Every single flower is ruined!

sentences.neutral: The volunteers will meet at the school at ten.
sentences.happy: You helped me, and it worked! I cannot thank you enough!
sentences.sad: You promised to help me. I waited, but I was truly on my own.
sentences.angry: You promised to help me and then vanished! You are completely unreliable!

sentences.neutral: The library holds about forty thousand books.
sentences.happy: They reopened the library! It is bigger and brighter than ever!
sentences.sad: They closed the old library. I spent my whole childhood in those rooms.
sentences.angry: They closed the library to build a parking lot! What a stupid decision!

sentences.neutral: The report states the facts of the case clearly.
sentences.happy: She told him the truth, and he forgave her! I am so relieved and glad!
sentences.sad: She told him the truth, and he never spoke to her again.
sentences.angry: She told him my secret! I trusted her, and she betrayed me!

sentences.neutral: The coffee machine is located on the second floor.
sentences.happy: The coffee is perfect! This is exactly what I needed this morning!
sentences.sad: The coffee went cold while I stared at the empty chair.
sentences.angry: The coffee is cold again! Does anyone in this place do their job?

sentences.neutral: The shower is on the first floor beside the bedroom.
sentences.happy: He sings in the shower, and it is hilarious! Everyone is laughing!
sentences.sad: He no longer sings in the shower. The whole house has gone quiet.
sentences.angry: Stop singing in the shower! It is six in the morning, for goodness sake!

sentences.neutral: Seat twelve is near the window on the left side.
sentences.happy: You are in my seat, but that is fine! Sit down, and enjoy the ride!
sentences.sad: You are in my seat. Honestly, I have no strength left to argue.
sentences.angry: You are in my seat! Get up right now, or I will call someone!

sentences.neutral: The store sells groceries, clothing, and household goods.
sentences.happy: The store is open late tonight! We can still get everything we need!
sentences.sad: The store closes at nine. After that, the whole street goes dark and still.
sentences.angry: The store closed in my face! I drove all the way here for nothing!

sentences.neutral: The bridge is nearly a mile long and made of steel.
sentences.happy: They built a bridge, and now our town is connected! What a great day!
sentences.sad: They built a bridge over the village that was lost. Nobody remembers it.
sentences.angry: They built the bridge right through my land! This is absolute robbery!

sentences.neutral: The phone is on the desk beside the lamp.
sentences.happy: The phone is ringing! I bet it is the good news we waited for!
sentences.sad: The phone rang twice, and then it fell silent. Nobody was there.
sentences.angry: The phone rang all night long! Whoever it was, I will find out!

sentences.neutral: The door leads out to the courtyard behind the house.
sentences.happy: The door is open, and the sun is pouring in! What a glorious day!
sentences.sad: She left the door open, hoping he would return. He never came back.
sentences.angry: You left the door open again! The whole house is freezing cold now!

sentences.neutral: The sun rises at six fifteen in the middle of summer.
sentences.happy: We watched the sunrise together! It was the most magical morning of my life!
sentences.sad: We watched the sunrise, and I knew it was our last one together.
sentences.angry: We watched the sunrise for nothing! The tour guide never even showed up!

sentences.neutral: The roof was replaced in the spring of last year.
sentences.happy: He fixed the roof! Now we can finally sleep without a single drip!
sentences.sad: He fixed the roof the day before the storm took everything away.
sentences.angry: He fixed the roof badly! Water is pouring into my living room!
